domains.name: Foundations (FND)
domains.description: The WIOA Title I participant journey in California, eligibility judgment and documentation, IEPs and case notes that survive validation, and structured onboarding for new AJCC staff.

domains.name: Registered Apprenticeship (APP)
domains.description: How Registered Apprenticeship works in California and nationally, apprenticeship-ready OJT contracts, braided funding, co-enrollment and coding, selling apprenticeship to employers, pre-apprenticeship on-ramps, and DAS registration.

domains.name: Apprenticeship Degrees (DEG)
domains.description: How apprenticeship hours and related instruction convert to college credit, California's apprenticeship-degree models, advising participants, and building degree-linked apprenticeships with education partners. Note: California's apprenticeship-degree landscape is early. AB 1904 (credentialed educator apprenticeships) and the Chancellor's Office Apprenticeship Pathway Demonstration Project are the anchors; a CSU or Apprenticeship Degree Network footprint was not verified. These courses should be refreshed as the field develops.

domains.name: SkillBridge and Veterans (VET)
domains.description: DoD SkillBridge for AJCC staff, routing transitioning service members and military spouses into Title I and apprenticeship, and helping employers become SkillBridge providers.

domains.name: Compliance and Quality (CMP)
domains.description: Data Element Validation readiness, the annual policy refresh on new and cancelled guidance, and monitoring-ready participant files and written procedures.

domains.name: Leadership and Operations (LDR)
domains.description: Process mapping an AJCC, AJCC certification and local plan evidence, surviving a provider transition, and building a board-level apprenticeship strategy.

subdomains.name: FND 101 — The Participant Journey: From Front Door to Follow-Up
subdomains.description: A walk through the complete WIOA Title I journey for Adult, Dislocated Worker, and Youth customers: sign-in, registration, eligibility, participation, services, outcomes, exit, follow-up, and validation. Each step is taught with who does it, what document it produces, and which rule governs it, using California's state spine and the learner's own local policy.

subdomains.name: FND 102 — Eligibility Judgment: Deciding, Documenting, Defending
subdomains.description: Eligibility errors are where monitoring findings start. This course covers the judgment calls the state Technical Assistance Guide (WSD24-04) leaves to staff: Dislocated Worker categories, "unlikely to return," self-attestation, low income, Selective Service, Youth school status, and priority of service. Learners practice on realistic case scenarios, including separating service members and apprentices.

subdomains.name: FND 103 — IEPs and Case Notes That Survive Validation
subdomains.description: Case-management practice is entirely local in California, and it is where turnover hurts most. Learners build an Individual Employment Plan (or Youth ISS) from an objective assessment, write case notes that document progress rather than opinion, and set activity dates that match real attendance.

subdomains.name: FND 104 — Your First 30 Days in an AJCC
subdomains.description: A self-paced onboarding sequence a board can assign on day one: how the workforce system is organized, who the partners are, where local policies live, what security and confidentiality training is required (WSD24-12), how to shadow effectively, and when to escalate. Modeled on Virginia's three-week case-manager learning path.

subdomains.name: APP 101 — Registered Apprenticeship for Workforce Professionals
subdomains.description: A plain-language foundation in how Registered Apprenticeship works in California and nationally, with emphasis on new-collar occupations in IT, healthcare, education, and advanced manufacturing. Covers the roles of DOL's Office of Apprenticeship and DAS, sponsors and intermediaries, IACA and CAC jurisdiction, related instruction, wage progression, and how apprenticeship fits inside WIOA.

subdomains.name: APP 102 — Writing Apprenticeship-Ready OJT Contracts and Cohort Training Plans
subdomains.description: California has no state OJT directive, and no local OJT template we found is built for a multi-year apprenticeship. This hands-on workshop teaches staff to write an OJT contract and a cohort training plan that fit apprenticeship: hours scaled to occupation, wage steps, reimbursement rates, the 90 percent small-employer waiver, combining OJT and ITA funds, employer documentation, and invoicing. Learners leave with a completed contract package and CCC's template toolkit.

subdomains.name: APP 103 — Braiding the Money: WIOA, AIF, RSI, CAI, and the GI Bill
subdomains.description: Who pays for what in an apprenticeship? This course maps every California and federal stream that can fund an apprentice or a program, the rules that prevent double-billing, and the sequence for stacking them. Includes a one-page braiding worksheet.

subdomains.name: APP 104 — Co-Enrollment and Coding: Making Apprentices Count
subdomains.description: Apprenticeship completions are recognized credentials and apprenticeship progress counts as Measurable Skill Gains, but only if staff enroll and code correctly. This course covers co-enrollment strategy, CalJOBS activity codes (300, 301, 428), PIRL element 931, type-of-training code 09, and how to capture outcomes over a multi-year apprenticeship.

subdomains.name: APP 105 — Selling Apprenticeship to Employers
subdomains.description: A consultative-selling workshop for workforce staff. Learners practice discovering an employer's hiring and skills problem, positioning apprenticeship (and OJT, incumbent worker training, or SkillBridge) as the solution, handling objections about cost and paperwork, and moving to a next step.

subdomains.name: APP 106 — Pre-Apprenticeship as an On-Ramp
subdomains.description: How to use pre-apprenticeship to move job seekers, especially youth and people with barriers, into Registered Apprenticeship. Covers quality pre-apprenticeship design, funding through ITAs when on the ETPL, counting youth pre-apprenticeship toward the 20 percent work experience requirement, and stipends under WSD23-08.

subdomains.name: APP 107 — Navigating DAS Registration
subdomains.description: A practical guide to getting a program and its apprentices registered in California: standards, the DAS 1 apprentice agreement, 8 CCR 206 timelines, IACA vs. CAC jurisdiction, and how intermediaries shorten the path. Sets realistic timeline expectations for employers.

subdomains.name: DEG 101 — Apprenticeship Degrees: Earning College Credit on the Job
subdomains.description: Apprenticeship degrees let a learner earn a paycheck, a journey-level credential, and college credit at the same time. This course explains the models (credit for related instruction, credit for prior learning, degree-embedded apprenticeships), California's current examples including teacher apprenticeships under AB 1904, and how to advise participants who want both a career and a degree.

subdomains.name: DEG 201 — Building Degree-Linked Apprenticeships with Education Partners
subdomains.description: For boards that want to move from referring to building. Covers convening an employer, a college, and a sponsor; aligning work processes with course outcomes; credit articulation; and funding the build through CAI, AIF, Regional Coordination Project funds (WSIN25-21), and WIOA.

subdomains.name: VET 101 — SkillBridge for AJCC Staff
subdomains.description: DoD SkillBridge lets service members spend their final 180 days of service training with an employer while still on military pay. This course explains how the program works, enrollment windows, provider obligations, and why AJCC staff should care: SkillBridge participants are the best-prepared Dislocated Workers and apprentices a center will ever see.

subdomains.name: VET 102 — From Uniform to Apprentice: Routing Transitioning Service Members
subdomains.description: A routing protocol for transitioning service members and military spouses. Covers veterans' priority of service, Dislocated Worker eligibility before separation, DVOP referral criteria, GI Bill approval checks for apprenticeship and OJT, and co-enrollment so the participant's outcomes count.

subdomains.name: VET 103 — Helping Employers Become SkillBridge Providers
subdomains.description: Most employers do not know they can host SkillBridge participants. This course teaches staff to coach an employer through becoming an authorized provider, pairing SkillBridge with a registered apprenticeship, and earning the HIRE Vets Medallion.

subdomains.name: CMP 201 — Data Element Validation Readiness
subdomains.description: Prepare for EDD's annual Data Element Validation. Covers the sampling process, the 15-business-day document window, source-document requirements (WSD22-15), the 10 percent error threshold, and a self-audit routine staff can run monthly.

subdomains.name: CMP 202 — Policy Refresh Clinic: What Changed in 2026
subdomains.description: An annual update that translates new and cancelled guidance into what staff do differently on Monday. The 2026 edition covers the cancellation of TEGL 09-22 (youth flexibilities), the rescission of TEGL 10-23 Change 2 (work authorization), the new ETPL directive WSD25-02, AJCC certification under WSD25-05, the 90 percent OJT waiver, and the CalJOBS modernization.

subdomains.name: CMP 203 — Monitoring-Ready Files and Procedures
subdomains.description: What monitors look for and how to be ready every day, not just the week before a visit. Covers WSD24-11 local monitoring standards, EO monitoring, file checklists, written procedures as evidence, and corrective action plans.

subdomains.name: LDR 301 — Process Mapping Your AJCC
subdomains.description: A working session where a center's team maps its own intake-to-exit process as swim lanes, marking the responsible role, artifact, and governing rule at each step, and flagging every step that lives only in someone's head. Uses CCC's statewide base map so teams start at 70 percent instead of zero.

subdomains.name: LDR 302 — AJCC Certification and Local Plan Evidence Workshop
subdomains.description: A deadline-driven workshop for the current certification and planning cycle. Focuses on certification indicator #6 ("high-quality, well-informed, and cross-trained staff") and the staff-training narrative required in local plan modifications due April 30, 2027. Learners leave with a draft evidence package and plan language.

subdomains.name: LDR 303 — Surviving a Provider Transition
subdomains.description: When a contract changes hands, knowledge walks out the door. Drawing on LA County's 2024 transition, this workshop covers knowledge transfer, caseload handoff, onboarding a new provider's staff, and protecting performance data during the gap.

subdomains.name: LDR 304 — Building an Apprenticeship Strategy for Your Board
subdomains.description: For leaders deciding how far into apprenticeship to go: referrer, navigator, intermediary, or sponsor. Covers TEGL 05-25 waiver opportunities, the 10 percent co-enrollment goal, navigator staffing models, the pending federal reauthorization, and California's apprenticeship funding streams.
